templates.recommendation: m6i/m7g (AWS) · n2-standard (GCP) · Dsv5 (Azure) — currently compute-leaning (0.49 vCPU/GiB, near compute-heavy boundary); c-families in mix acceptable

critical.finding: 2x r6a.large nodes: EKS ENI formula caps them at 29 pods, but static kubeletConfig.maxPods=55 in node configuration ngm-kronos-castai (v31) — pods can be scheduled on these nodes with no IPs left (ContainerCreating / IP exhaustion risk). Only 45% of CPU is allocatable on these 2-vCPU nodes.
critical.action: Lower kubelet maxPods to <=29 for small instances (or remove the static override), and set minCpu>=4 in the node template so 2-vCPU nodes are never provisioned.

high.finding: [INFORMATIONAL] 93.7% of requested CPU is wasted (38 of 41 cores unused, workload-efficiency 30d); 264 WOOP-managed workloads (6 policies, ORIGIN_ASSIGNMENT_RULES) but all recommendation statuses STATUS_UNKNOWN / appliedPods=0 — WOOP not yet applying. WOOP agent v1.10.4 is behind latest v1.14.1.
high.action: Upgrade workload-autoscaler to v1.14.1 and verify why recommendations are not applying (appliedPods=0) before relying on WOOP savings.

high.finding: [INFORMATIONAL] Cluster collapses to 3 nodes (~14 vCPU) on weekends (3-104 nodes over 30d) — idle-standby dev pattern; ~$0.3k/mo weekend hibernation candidate. Unscheduled pods = 0 verified.
high.action: Schedule weekend scale-down / hibernation (e.g. castai pause or scheduled node-count reduction) for this dev cluster.

high.finding: [INFORMATIONAL] Live pod-health scan (Pending/Failed/CrashLoopBackOff) could not be performed — no kubectl access (AWS credentials expired at collection time). Proxies show: unscheduled pods = 0, problematic nodes = 1 (removal-disabled only), 0 WOOP problematic pods.
high.action: Re-run Steps 4-5 with live kubectl/API access to confirm container-level health.

medium.finding: Single default template with spot OFF: nodeConstraints maxCpu=16 but no minCpu/minMemory floor (unlike sibling cluster helios); spotInterruptionPredictions enabled with deprecated type aws-rebalance-recommendations.
medium.action: Add minCpu/minMemory floors to the template; when spot is enabled for dev, migrate prediction type from aws-rebalance-recommendations to the native CAST AI spot prediction model.

medium.finding: [INFORMATIONAL] Evictor enabled but reported Not-Allowed / Incompatible on this self-managed cluster (cluster-autoscaler deployment still present, evictor-advanced config empty). 12 drains / 16 node deletions in the audit window were rebalancer-driven. 19/50 recent rebalancing plans ended achievedSavingsBelowThreshold — benign schedule-skip condition, excluded from blocked nodes.
medium.action: Remove/disable the legacy cluster-autoscaler deployment and make evictor compatible to unlock continuous consolidation.

medium.finding: No minCpu floor: 2-vCPU r6a.large nodes carry the full per-node DaemonSet/system tax (only 0.9 of 2.0 vCPU allocatable). DaemonSet requests = 510m of 6.06 vCPU workload requests (8.4%) on a 14-node cluster, so the >=50-node advisory does not fire but the tax is material on small instances.
medium.action: Set minCpu=4 in node template default-by-castai to avoid tiny nodes absorbing full DaemonSet overhead.
